title: Graphic texts: evaluating the techniques used

blocks.content: Media makers use clever techniques to grab you and win you over. A smart reader can name these techniques and judge how well they work.
Media techniques include slogans, bright colours, and famous faces — all used to attract attention and persuade.

steps: An advert has a short catchy line: 'Taste the sunshine!'
That short, memorable phrase is a slogan.
It is a technique to make the product stick in your mind.

blocks.question: Why does an advert use a famous sports star to hold the product?
options: to make you trust and want the product
blocks.explain: A famous, admired face is a technique to make you trust and want the product.
blocks.rule: Media techniques like slogans, colour and famous faces are used to attract attention and persuade.

practiceItems.prompt: a short, catchy phrase in an advert is a ___
a famous face is used to make you ___ the product (trust/ignore)
bright colours are used to grab your ___
'Taste the sunshine!' is an example of a ___

blocks.content: To evaluate a media text is to judge how well its techniques work — and to say why.

blocks.question: Evaluating an advert means:
options: judging how well its techniques work and why
blocks.explain: Evaluating is judging how effective the techniques are, with reasons.
blocks.rule: To evaluate a media text is to judge how well its techniques work, with reasons.

practiceItems.prompt: judging how well an advert works is to ___ it (evaluate/copy)
a catchy phrase technique is a ___
bright colour is a technique to grab ___
an evaluation should give a judgement and a ___

blocks.content: Name the techniques — slogans, colour, famous faces — then judge how well they work. That is evaluating media. Let's practise!
